problems.title: Pipe-bend sofa
problems.words: A round pipe of diameter 1 bends at a right angle. What is the biggest solid that fits around the bend?
problems.math: Maximize volume over rigid-motion-admissible solids in the union of two half-cylinders of diameter 1 meeting at a right angle.

problems.title: Hyperbolic square peg
problems.words: Every closed curve in the hyperbolic plane should pass through the corners of some hyperbolic square.
problems.math: Prove every Jordan curve in $\mathbb{H}^2$ contains the four vertices of a regular hyperbolic quadrilateral.

problems.title: Square-sum cliques
problems.words: How many numbers can pairwise add up to perfect squares? Decide if there is a limit.
problems.math: Decide whether $\omega(S_N)$ is bounded, i.e., whether there exist arbitrarily large sets of distinct positive integers with all pairwise sums square.

problems.title: Largest-factor Collatz stopping time
problems.words: How many steps does the largest-factor Collatz map take, on average, to reach 1?
problems.math: Prove $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}T(n)\sim c\log x$ for the stopping time $T$ of $f$, and compute $c$.

problems.title: Zigzag sofa
problems.words: A hallway turns right, then left after distance d. Find the best sofa for every d.
problems.math: For each $d>0$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with two opposite right turns separated by $d$.

problems.title: Hat spectrum is a Cantor set
problems.words: Show the energy levels of a particle hopping on a hat tiling form a dust of measure zero.
problems.math: Prove the spectrum of the adjacency operator on the hat graph is a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero.

problems.title: 5n+1 largest-factor cycles
problems.words: Use 5n + 1 instead of 3n + 1 in the largest-factor map. Show it has only finitely many loops.
problems.math: For $f_5(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(5n+1)$ (odd), prove $f_5$ has finitely many cycles.

problems.title: Lonely runners in 3D
problems.words: Runners move in three dimensions on a cube that wraps around. Find the guaranteed loneliness.
problems.math: For $n$ pairwise independent $v_i\in\mathbb{Z}^3$, find the optimal $\delta_n$ with $\sup_t\min_i\|tv_i\|_{\mathbb{T}^3,\infty}\ge\delta_n$.

problems.title: Spectre percolation
problems.words: Show percolation on the spectre tiling and the hat tiling have different thresholds.
problems.math: Prove $p_c^{\text{site}}(\text{spectre})\ne p_c^{\text{site}}(\text{hat})$.

problems.title: Self-similar fire
problems.words: Show a fire spreading with random fuel forms a shape that grows at a fixed limiting speed in every direction.
problems.math: For first-passage percolation on the hat graph with i.i.d. exponential weights, prove the limit shape exists and is not a polygon.

problems.title: Smallest-factor Collatz stopping time
problems.words: How many steps does the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map take to reach 1, on average?
problems.math: Determine the asymptotic order of $\frac1x\sum_{n\le x}T_g(n)$ for the stopping time of $g$.

problems.title: Midpoint map as a random walk
problems.words: Show that, for a random large start, the logarithm of the midpoint-prime orbit moves like a Gaussian random walk.
problems.math: Prove that for $n$ uniform in $[x,2x]$, the distribution of $\log m^{k}(n)-\log n$ for $k=\lfloor\log x\rfloor$ converges after normalization to a Gaussian.

problems.title: Greedy independent sets in square sums
problems.words: Pick random numbers up to N one by one, skipping any that sum to a square with something already picked. How many do you end with?
problems.math: Determine the asymptotic size of the random greedy independent set in $S_N$, in probability.

problems.title: Hamiltonian cycles in hat patches
problems.words: Count closed tours visiting every tile of a large hat-tiled region once. Find the exponential growth rate per tile.
problems.math: For hat-tiled $L$-balls with $n$ tiles, prove $(\#\text{Hamiltonian cycles})^{1/n}\to\beta$ and determine $\beta$ to 3 digits rigorously.

problems.title: Hats in a torus
problems.words: Hats tile the plane only non-periodically, so they cannot tile a flat torus. Find the smallest uncovered fraction for packing hats on a flat torus of area A.
problems.math: Let $g(A)$ be the least uncovered area over packings of congruent hats in flat tori of area $A$. Prove $g(A)\to\infty$ and determine its growth order in $A$.

problems.title: Discrete sofa
problems.words: Slide and rotate a polyomino by unit steps and quarter turns around the corner of a corridor k cells wide. Find the largest area possible, asymptotically.
problems.math: Let $D(k)$ be the maximal number of cells of a polyomino that can pass the width-$k$ L-shaped corridor of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ by unit translations and $90^\circ$ rotations about lattice points (staying inside at all times). Prove $D(k)\sim ck^2$ and find $c$.

problems.title: Hard-core on the hat
problems.words: Place particles on hat tiles with no two neighbours both occupied. Show the gas freezes into an ordered state at high density.
problems.math: For the hard-core model on the hat graph, prove a phase transition: non-uniqueness of Gibbs measures for all activities $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$.

problems.title: Square-plus-one collisions
problems.words: Count pairs n ≠ m up to x for which n² + 1 and m² + 1 have the same largest prime factor.
problems.math: Find the asymptotic number of pairs $n<m\le x$ with $P(n^2+1)=P(m^2+1)$.

problems.title: Alternating prime residues
problems.words: Find ten consecutive primes whose remainders mod 4 alternate 1, 3, 1, 3, …, and infinitely many such runs.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $p_{n+i}\equiv 2+(-1)^{i}\pmod 4$ for $0\le i<10$.

problems.title: Hat tiling Lee–Yang zeros
problems.words: For magnets on a hat tiling, show the complex zeros of the partition function pinch the real axis at exactly one point.
problems.math: Prove the Lee–Yang zeros of the ferromagnetic Ising model on growing hat patches accumulate on the positive real temperature axis only at $\beta_c$.

problems.title: Largest-factor cycles
problems.words: Find every loop of the largest-factor Collatz map.
problems.math: Prove every periodic orbit of $f(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(3n+1)$ (odd) lies in an explicit finite list, and give it.

problems.title: Emirp twins
problems.words: Show infinitely many twin-prime pairs exist where both reverse to primes, assuming only standard sieve bounds plus one level-of-distribution hypothesis.
problems.math: Assuming Elliott–Halberstam, prove infinitely many $p$ with $p,p+2,\operatorname{rev}(p),\operatorname{rev}(p+2)$ prime among bounded gaps of tuples $(p,p+h)$, $h\le H$ explicit.

problems.title: Lonely runners with square speeds
problems.words: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when all speeds are perfect squares.
problems.math: For distinct positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_n$, prove $\sup_t\min_i\|ta_i^2\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$.

problems.title: 4p+1 maximal climbs
problems.words: Show the 4p + 1 prime map can climb arbitrarily high above its starting point before falling into its loop.
problems.math: Prove $\sup_p \max_k P_4^k(p)/p=\infty$, where $P_4(p)=P(4p+1)$.

problems.title: Lattice gauge on the hat
problems.words: Show the Z/2 lattice gauge theory on a hat-tiled surface times a line has a deconfinement transition.
problems.math: For $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory on the 3D cell complex $\mathrm{hat}\times\mathbb{Z}$, prove the Wilson loop changes from area law to perimeter law at a single critical coupling.

problems.title: Prime cubes with one shift
problems.words: Show infinitely many quadruples of primes satisfy x³ + y³ = z³ + w³ + 1.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many prime solutions $(x,y,z,w)$ of $x^3+y^3=z^3+w^3+1$.

problems.title: Lonely runner gap for the first n primes
problems.words: For the first n primes as speeds, find the actual loneliness gap asymptotically.
problems.math: Determine the asymptotics of $\delta_n=\sup_t\min_{i\le n}\|tp_i\|$ as $n\to\infty$.

problems.title: Long progressions of seven-free primes
problems.words: Show the seven-free primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
problems.math: Prove for every $k$ there are $k$-term arithmetic progressions consisting of primes with no decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Few periodic points of square-plus-one
problems.words: Count the numbers up to X that lie on a loop of the square-plus-one map. Show there are very few.
problems.math: Prove $\#\{n\le X: Q^k(n)=n\text{ for some }k\ge1\}=X^{o(1)}$, where $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$.

problems.title: Finitely many loops for affine prime maps
problems.words: For fixed a and b, show the prime map p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + b has only finitely many loops.
problems.math: Prove that for all integers $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, the map $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ on primes has finitely many periodic orbits.

problems.title: Largest factor of shifted primes mod 4
problems.words: For primes p, look at the largest prime factor of p − 1. Show it is 1 mod 4 exactly half the time.
problems.math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: P(p-1)\equiv1\ (4)\}\sim\tfrac12\pi(x)$.

problems.title: Spanning trees inside the square-sum graph
problems.words: Show every tree of maximum degree 3 on N vertices fits inside the square-sum graph on 1 to N.
problems.math: Prove every tree on $N\ge N_0$ vertices with maximum degree $\le3$ is a spanning subgraph of $S_N$.

problems.title: Seven-free primes in Piatetski-Shapiro sequences
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes of the form ⌊n^1.1⌋ have no digit 7.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $\lfloor n^{1.1}\rfloor$ free of the decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Sofa beyond Gerver in 3 dimensions of turning
problems.words: A 2D hallway that turns 90° twice in a row (an S-bend): find the best sofa.
problems.math: Determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with two consecutive right turns in opposite directions, separated by length $L$, for every $L>0$.

problems.title: Optimal sofa is not algebraic anywhere
problems.words: Show the optimal sofa for a 60° turn has an outline that no polynomial equation describes.
problems.math: Prove the boundary of the optimal sofa for the $60^\circ$ corridor contains no arc of any algebraic curve.

problems.title: Prime necklaces for all n
problems.words: Arrange 1 to 2n in a circle so every two neighbours sum to a prime, and so do every two numbers three apart.
problems.math: Prove for all large $n$ a cyclic arrangement of $[2n]$ with $\pi_i+\pi_{i+1}$ and $\pi_i+\pi_{i+3}$ prime for all $i$.

problems.title: Spectral gap of the spectre
problems.words: Find the exact gaps in the energy levels of an electron moving on a spectre tiling.
problems.math: Prove the spectrum of the adjacency operator on the spectre tiling has gaps labelled by an explicit $K$-theory group, with every label open.

problems.title: Polykite growth is irrational
problems.words: Show the growth rate of polykite counts is an irrational number.
problems.math: Prove $\lambda=\lim k_n^{1/n}$ for polykites is irrational.

problems.title: Three of four
problems.words: Show infinitely often at least three of the four doubled-twin numbers are prime at once.
problems.math: Prove there are infinitely many $n$ such that at least three of $n,n+2,2n+1,2n+3$ are prime.

problems.title: Sofa for every corridor
problems.words: Give one method that finds the best sofa for every hallway shape.
problems.math: Prove optimal sofas for piecewise-linear corridors are characterized by a finite system of ODEs on boundary arcs, and solve it in closed form for all right-angle corridors of width ratio $r$.

problems.title: Chess on the hat board
problems.words: Solve a chess-like game on a hat-tiled board with 10 pieces per side.
problems.math: Weakly solve the game with standard chess move semantics translated to the hat graph on a fixed 64-tile patch.

problems.title: Toroidal Go 9×9
problems.words: Who wins Go on a 9×9 board that wraps around in both directions?
problems.math: Weakly solve Go on $\mathbb{Z}_9^2$ with area scoring and komi $0$.

problems.title: Polykite complete classification
problems.words: For every polykite, decide whether it tiles, and if so how.
problems.math: Give an algorithm deciding, for any single polykite, whether it tiles the plane, and prove it correct.

problems.title: Fewest burned cells
problems.words: In the wind-driven fire (spreading only east, north and south), with the fewest firefighters that can trap it, what is the least area that must burn?
problems.math: For the minimal $k$ in the east/north/south fire on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, find $\min |B_\infty|$ over all protection strategies.

problems.title: Shuffle with a cut
problems.words: Do a perfect shuffle, then cut k cards from top to bottom, and repeat. How many repetitions bring the deck back?
problems.math: For the permutation $c_k\circ\sigma_{\text{out}}$ on $2n$ cards, determine its order as a function of $n$ and $k$.

problems.title: Delayed firefighters
problems.words: Fire spreads in four directions, but a firefighter assigned now only takes effect a turn later. How many per turn are needed?
problems.math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with 4-neighbour spread, cells chosen at turn $t$ become protected at turn $t+1$. Find the least per-turn number that contains a single fire.

problems.title: Blank jigsaw
problems.words: A jigsaw with no picture can only be solved from piece shapes. How few edge shapes force a unique solution?
problems.math: Find the asymptotics in $n$ of the least number of edge types such that some $n\times n$ jigsaw has exactly one assembly (up to rotation of the whole).

problems.title: Penrose firefighter
problems.words: Fire spreads along a Penrose tiling's edges. How many firefighters per turn can trap any fire?
problems.math: On the vertex graph of a Penrose rhomb tiling, find the least $k$ such that protecting $k$ vertices per turn contains a fire from any single vertex.

problems.title: Three-pile shuffle group
problems.words: Using the six ways to stack three piles in a perfect shuffle, which rearrangements of the deck can you reach?
problems.math: Determine the subgroup of $S_{3n}$ generated by the six 3-pile perfect shuffles (all pile orders), for every $n$.

problems.title: Shortest proof that √2 is irrational
problems.words: Find the shortest possible Lean proof that the square root of 2 is irrational, and prove nothing shorter works.
problems.math: Over Lean 4 core tactics on top of Mathlib's definitions, find the minimal tactic-step proof of `Irrational (Real.sqrt 2)` and certify minimality.

problems.title: Toroidal Hex
problems.words: Hex on a doughnut: the board wraps around, and you win with a chain that loops the long way. Who wins on 7 × 7?
problems.math: On the $7\times7$ Hex board with opposite sides identified, a player wins with a non-contractible chain of their colour; determine the winner and whether draws occur.

problems.title: Formalize the sofa
problems.words: Turn Baek's proof that Gerver's sofa is optimal into a computer-checked proof.
problems.math: Formalize in Lean 4 the statement and proof that the moving sofa constant equals the area of Gerver's sofa.

problems.title: Percolation on the hat tiling
problems.words: Each hat tile is open at random with probability p. Find where an infinite open cluster first appears.
problems.math: For site percolation on the hat adjacency graph, prove $0.6<p_c<0.7$ (or the correct interval) with rigorous bounds.

problems.title: Optimal origami base
problems.words: Folders design animal shapes by packing circles on paper. Find the smallest paper needed for every stick figure with six legs or fewer.
problems.math: For every weighted tree with $\le6$ leaves, determine the minimum square side admitting a uniaxial base (optimal circle–river packing), with certificates.

problems.title: Equal-area triangles in the hat
problems.words: Cut the hat tile into triangles of equal area. Which numbers of triangles are possible?
problems.math: Determine the set of $n$ for which the hat polygon admits a dissection into $n$ triangles of equal area.

problems.title: Toroidal Sudoku
problems.words: Sudoku where the 3 × 3 boxes wrap around the board's edges. What is the fewest clues for a unique solution?
problems.math: For the $9\times9$ Sudoku variant whose box regions are a fixed partition into wrapped $3\times3$ blocks on $\mathbb{Z}_9^2$, find the minimum number of givens.

problems.title: No prism sofa
problems.words: Show the best 3D sofa is genuinely three-dimensional, not just a flat shape extruded upward.
problems.math: Prove no optimal solid for the $1\times1$ square corridor is of the form $A\times[0,1]$.

problems.title: Seven-free primes in progressions
problems.words: Primes avoiding the digit 7 should be evenly spread among remainder classes.
problems.math: Prove primes without decimal digit 7 are equidistributed in residue classes mod $q$ for all $q\le(\log x)^A$.

problems.title: Tangent-sweep Keller maps
problems.words: One 2026 counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture sweeps tangent lines of a curve. Find every counterexample built that way.
problems.math: Classify all polynomial maps $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with constant nonzero Jacobian arising from the tangent-sweep construction over plane curves.

problems.title: Prime-frequency synchrony
problems.words: Oscillators with frequencies set by logarithms of primes eventually synchronize when coupled strongly enough. Find the threshold.
problems.math: For the Kuramoto model with $\omega_i=\log p_i$, prove a sharp synchronization threshold $K_c(N)$ and its asymptotics.

problems.title: Four colors, compressed
problems.words: Make the computer-checked four color theorem much shorter.
problems.math: Give a Lean 4 proof of the four color theorem in under 20,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

problems.title: Firefighters on the front line
problems.words: Firefighters may only protect cells touching the fire. How many per turn are needed now?
problems.math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with protected cells required to be 4-adjacent to the burned set, find the least per-turn number containing a single fire.

problems.title: Fire on a random tree
problems.words: On a tree where each node has three branches, fire jumps to two random branches per step. Can one firefighter per turn win?
problems.math: On the 3-ary tree with fire spreading to a uniform random 2 of 3 children each step, compute $\Pr(\text{containment})$ with one protection per turn.

problems.title: Undecidable polykite tiling
problems.words: For sets of five shapes made of kites, deciding whether they tile the plane is unsolvable by any algorithm.
problems.math: Prove that tileability of $\mathbb{R}^2$ by finite sets of at most 5 polykites is undecidable.

problems.title: Fire whirls
problems.words: Show the equations of buoyant flow allow a rotating column of fire that travels steadily.
problems.math: Prove existence of a smooth traveling swirling solution of the 3D Boussinesq equations with a localized heat source.

problems.title: Prime Langford pairings
problems.words: Arrange two copies each of 1 to n so the two copies of k sit exactly the k-th prime apart. For which n is this possible?
problems.math: Determine all $n$ for which $1,1,\dots,n,n$ can be arranged so the two copies of $k$ are $p_k$ positions apart.

problems.title: Navier–Stokes blow-up in Isabelle
problems.words: Re-check the 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up in a completely different proof assistant.
problems.math: Formalize in Isabelle/HOL the existence of a smooth forced finite-time blow-up of 3D Navier–Stokes.

problems.title: Unit-distance barrier
problems.words: Show the 2026 number-field method for many equal distances can never reach exponent 1.1.
problems.math: Prove every construction of the Alon–Bloom–Gowers–…–Sawin type (lattices from number fields of bounded class-field degree) gives $u(n)\le n^{1.1}$.

problems.title: Hat treewidth
problems.words: Find exactly how hard hat-tiled regions are to break into small pieces.
problems.math: Prove the treewidth of $n$-tile hat patches is $\sim c\sqrt n$ and compute $c$.

problems.title: Four-arc sofa
problems.words: Find the best sofa whose outline uses at most four circular arcs and straight pieces.
problems.math: Maximize area over admissible sofas whose boundary consists of at most four circular arcs plus segments.

problems.title: Hat corona limit
problems.words: Surround a hat by layers of hats again and again. The growing blob approaches a fixed shape. Find it.
problems.math: Prove the scaled $k$-th coronas of a hat converge in Hausdorff distance and identify the limit shape.

problems.title: Gerver sofa contact points
problems.words: Prove Gerver's sofa touches the corridor walls in exactly the pattern Gerver described at every moment of its optimal motion, and that the motion is unique.
problems.math: Prove the optimal motion of Gerver's sofa through the unit corridor is unique up to time reparametrization.

problems.title: Maker–Breaker square-sum triangles
problems.words: Maker and Breaker alternately claim numbers. Maker wins by owning three numbers whose pairwise sums are all squares. Decide who wins on 1 to N for large N.
problems.math: Determine the winner of the Maker–Breaker game on $[N]$ whose winning sets are the triangles of $S_N$, for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: Stable blow-up
problems.words: Show the 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up still happens after any tiny change to the setup.
problems.math: Prove the 2026 forced blow-up is stable under small smooth perturbations of $(u_0,f)$ in a suitable topology.

problems.title: Galois groups of Keller fibers
problems.words: Find the symmetry group of the preimages of a point under the 2026 Keller maps.
problems.math: Compute the Galois group of the generic fiber of Gallagher's degree-$n$ Keller family for each $n\ge3$.

problems.title: Symmetric sofa
problems.words: Find the best sofa that is symmetric under a half-turn.
problems.math: Maximize area over centrally symmetric sets admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor.

problems.title: Hyperoperation fixed points
problems.words: In any natural real-rank hyperoperation family, show the rank at which 2 ∘ 2 stops being 4 is not a whole number.
problems.math: For the unique analytic family $a[s]b$ satisfying the recursion and log-convexity in $s$, prove $\{s: 2[s]2=4\}$ is exactly $[1,\infty)\cap$ an explicit closed set and determine whether it is an interval.

problems.title: Rational fibres of the Alpöge map
problems.words: The 2026 Jacobian counterexample sends three rational points to one point. Show infinitely many rational target points have three rational preimages.
problems.math: For Alpöge's Keller map $F:\mathbb{Q}^3\to\mathbb{Q}^3$, prove $\{y\in\mathbb{Q}^3:|F^{-1}(y)\cap\mathbb{Q}^3|=3\}$ is Zariski dense in $\mathbb{A}^3$.

problems.title: Cube-sum Hamiltonian cycles
problems.words: Arrange 1 to N in a circle so neighbours add to perfect cubes, for all large N.
problems.math: Prove $C_N$ is Hamiltonian for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: 3-pile shuffle mixing constant
problems.words: Find the exact cutoff constant for riffle-style 3-pile shuffles, in closed form.
problems.math: For random 3-pile shuffles on $3n$ cards, prove cutoff at $c\log n$ with $c$ in closed form and window $O(1)$.

problems.title: Hyperoperation at rank 2.5 is transcendental
problems.words: Show 2 combined with 3 at "rank 2.5" in the natural hyperoperation family is transcendental.
problems.math: For the unique natural family $a[s]b$, prove $2[2.5]3$ is transcendental.

problems.title: Waring with seven-free cubes
problems.words: Find the fewest cubes of seven-free numbers needed to write every large number, and prove it.
problems.math: Determine the least $s$ such that every sufficiently large integer is a sum of $s$ cubes of positive 7-free integers.

problems.title: Spectre hard hexagons
problems.words: Show the hard-core gas on the spectre tiling has exactly one phase transition, at a single sharp activity.
problems.math: Prove the hard-core model on the spectre adjacency graph has a unique critical activity $\lambda_c$ with uniqueness for $\lambda<\lambda_c$ and non-uniqueness for $\lambda>\lambda_c$.

problems.title: Digit-restricted Chowla
problems.words: Show μ(n)μ(n+1) has no bias on numbers n where neither n nor n+1 contains the digit 7.
problems.math: Prove $\sum_{n\le x,\ 7\notin n,\ 7\notin n+1}\mu(n)\mu(n+1)=o(x^{\log9/\log10})$.

problems.title: The 3p+4 seven-cycle
problems.words: Send a prime p to the largest prime factor of 3p + 4. Every prime tested ends in the loop 11 → 37 → 23 → 73 → 223 → 673 → 17 → 11. Prove all do.
problems.math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(3p+4)$ on primes enters the cycle $(11,37,23,73,223,673,17)$.

problems.title: The 5p+4 nine-cycle
problems.words: For p ↦ largest prime factor of 5p + 4, every tested prime ends in one loop of nine primes through 11. Prove all do.
problems.math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(5p+4)$ on primes enters the cycle $(11,59,23,17,89,449,173,79,19)$.

problems.title: Critical Ising on the hat is SLE(3)
problems.words: Show the interface in the critical Ising model on a hat tiling converges to the random curve SLE(3), even though the graph is not isoradial.
problems.math: For the critical Ising model on the hat graph with Dobrushin boundary conditions, prove the interface converges to chordal SLE$_3$.

problems.title: Critical hat Ising temperature is irrational
problems.words: Show the critical temperature of the Ising model on a hat tiling is not a rational multiple of the coupling.
problems.math: Prove $\beta_c J\notin\mathbb{Q}$ for the ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph.

problems.title: Hat Hofstadter gaps all open
problems.words: Show every gap predicted by the gap-labelling theorem actually opens in the hat tiling's electronic spectrum.
problems.math: Prove the dry ten-Martini property for the vertex adjacency operator of the hat tiling: every gap label in the $K_0$-group of the hull corresponds to an open gap.

problems.title: Square-plus-one merging
problems.words: Many square-plus-one sequences run into the one starting at 2. Decide whether every sequence eventually does, apart from those caught in loops.
problems.math: Decide whether every $n\ge2$ whose $Q$-orbit is not eventually periodic satisfies $Q^a(n)=Q^b(2)$ for some $a,b$.

problems.title: Irrational orbit sum
problems.words: Add the reciprocals of the square-plus-one sequence starting from 2. Show the total is irrational.
problems.math: Prove $\sum_{k\ge0}1/Q^k(2)$ converges and is irrational.

problems.title: Simple spectrum of the hat
problems.words: Show no two vibration frequencies of the hat-shaped drum coincide.
problems.math: Prove every Dirichlet eigenvalue of the hat polygon is simple.

problems.title: Conformal radius of the hat
problems.words: Map a disc conformally onto the hat so the centre goes to the hat's centroid. Show the scale factor is transcendental.
problems.math: Prove the conformal radius of the hat polygon at its centroid is transcendental.

problems.title: Spectre self-avoiding walks
problems.words: Find the exponential growth rate of non-self-intersecting walks on the spectre tiling, and show it is the same for every spectre tiling.
problems.math: Prove the connective constant $\mu$ of the spectre adjacency graph exists, is the same for all spectre tilings, and is not algebraic of degree $\le2$.

problems.title: Strict convexity of hat first-passage
problems.words: Give each hat-tile edge an independent random length. Prove the limiting ball of first-passage distances is strictly convex.
problems.math: For i.i.d. continuous edge weights with finite exponential moment on the hat adjacency graph, prove the first-passage limit shape exists and is strictly convex.

problems.title: Exponential growth of square-plus-one orbits
problems.words: Show square-plus-one sequences, when they don't loop, grow at a steady exponential rate in the number of digits.
problems.math: Prove that for almost every $n$ (density 1), $\lim_{k}\frac1k\log\log Q^k(n)$ exists and equals a constant $\gamma>0$; identify $\gamma$.

problems.title: Hat percolation is conformally invariant
problems.words: Show critical percolation on the hat tiling's tiles has crossing probabilities given by Cardy's formula.
problems.math: For critical site percolation on hat tiles, prove crossing probabilities of conformal rectangles converge to Cardy's formula as the mesh $\to0$.

problems.title: Gerver constant is normal
